issue.close_reason: Implemented staleness warning for rates.json - added reviewedThrough field (2026-07-01) and display warning banner when rates are 6+ months old, making staleness visible to end users without external monitoring
issue.description:
public/rates.json's meta.asOf currently reads 'current as of 2026-07' as free-text prose with no machine-checkable date, and public/calc.js's caveats already admit 'Absolute totals are +/-~5%... 2026 months are priced at 2025 rates.' ConEd revises SC1/TOU/demand rates via PSC rate cases roughly annually; nothing here catches the tool quietly going stale.

Add a machine-readable field to rates.json, e.g. "reviewedThrough": "2026-07-01" alongside the existing meta.asOf prose. In public/app.js, compare that date to the current date at render time; if more than ~6 months have elapsed, show a small non-blocking banner ('Rates last verified 2026-07 -- may be out of date; treat as directional') in the results view, similar in style to the existing .legend notes. This makes staleness visible to end users immediately (no external monitoring infra needed) and gives the maintainer a concrete prompt to refresh public/rates.json + bump reviewedThrough on the next pass.
issue.title: Show an on-page warning when rates.json hasn't been reviewed in 6+ months

issue.close_reason: Added automated test suite and committed sample Green Button CSV fixture. test/test.js covers 16 tests (parsing, analysis, rate calculations, edge cases) and verify.js now runs successfully from a clean checkout. All tests passing (16/16).
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-47y, 2026-07-30T03:14:01.794631661Z, author cli]
GAP (plan-vs-artifacts): calc.js is the non-trivial core -- a hand-rolled CSV parser (parseGreenButton), an ESPI/Green Button XML parser (parseESPI), a client-side ZIP inflater (unzipCsv), and four cost models (costStandard, costTOU, costDemand x2). None of it has any automated test.

Evidence:
- No test/spec files exist anywhere in the repo (find for *test*/*spec* returns nothing; no .github, no committed CI).
- verify.js line 6 defaults its input path to HOME + /scratch/coned/electricty.csv -- a file that is NOT in the repo. From a clean checkout, node verify.js fails with ENOENT, so the README "Verify the math" step is not runnable by anyone cloning the repo.
- public/sample.js exercises analyze() on pre-aggregated monthly totals only; it bypasses all three parser paths entirely, so the most bug-prone code (CSV/XML/ZIP parsing) has zero coverage of any kind.

This is distinct from bf-41r (that bead is about verify.js not applying rates.json, not about the absence of tests/fixtures).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A small, anonymized Green Button CSV fixture (a few days of interval rows) is committed under the repo (e.g. test/fixtures/) so parser tests run without any external file.
- An automated test (plain node script or a lightweight runner) asserts: (a) parseGreenButton produces expected interval/day counts and monthly peak/off split on the fixture; (b) analyze() yields the expected Standard vs TOU verdict/totals within tolerance; ideally (c) a tiny ESPI XML fixture round-trips through parseESPI.
- verify.js either defaults to the committed fixture (or documents the external-file requirement) so node verify.js succeeds from a clean checkout.
- The test is runnable via a single documented command (README updated) and, once ADR-001 push-to-deploy lands (bf-6v7), can be wired as a pre-deploy check.
issue.title: No automated tests / committed fixture for calc.js core; verify.js can't run from a clean checkout

issue.description:
public/index.html already has a well-formed FAQ section (section.faq, 4 Q&A pairs: 'Is ConEd Time-of-Use worth it?', 'What are Steady Use and Smart Energy?', 'Is there a ConEd EV rate?', 'Is my data private?') but no structured data markup. Adding a <script type='application/ld+json'> FAQPage schema (schema.org) referencing the same Q&A text is a small, mechanical change with real upside: Google can render these as expandable rich-result snippets in search for queries like 'is coned time of use worth it', which is likely to meaningfully increase organic click-through for a site with essentially zero paid-acquisition budget.

Keep the JSON-LD text in sync with the visible h3/p content in section.faq (or generate it from the same source at build time if a build step is ever added) so they can't drift apart -- real-world FAQ schema implementations get penalized by Google if they do.

issue.close_reason: Added Cloudflare Web Analytics (cookie-less, privacy-safe) to measure site usage. issue.description:
The site has no analytics of any kind -- there is currently no way to know if anyone visits coned.jedarden.com, or what fraction of visitors get as far as uploading a file vs. bouncing on the landing page. Cloudflare Web Analytics (free, already the hosting platform via CF Pages) is cookie-less and doesn't fingerprint, so it doesn't conflict with the page's existing privacy claim ('nothing is uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere') -- that claim is specifically about the user's uploaded usage data, not standard pageview counting.

Add the CF Web Analytics beacon snippet to public/index.html (or enable it directly in the Cloudflare Pages project settings, no code change needed) and, if it's easy to do without touching user data, a custom event on the 'Try it with a sample home' button click and on successful file parse (public/app.js render()) vs. parse error (showError()) -- this gives a real funnel: visits -> sample-tried -> real-file-uploaded -> error-rate, all without ever transmitting the file contents or the computed result. Note in README.md or the footer that anonymous, cookie-less visit analytics are collected, for transparency.
issue.title: Add Cloudflare Web Analytics (cookie-less) to measure whether coned.jedarden.com is actually used

issue.close_reason: Fixed verify.js to load public/rates.json and call calc.applyRates() before analysis, matching the live browser tool's runtime behavior. This ensures Node verification validates against the same rate data that users see, preventing silent divergence if future edits update rates.json without updating calc.js defaults. Added a startup assertion that warns when rates.json values differ from baked-in defaults, making drift visible during verification.
issue.description:
public/app.js fetches public/rates.json at runtime and overrides calc.js's baked-in RATES defaults (public/calc.js applyRates()) -- this is the actual rate data the live browser tool uses. verify.js (the Node sanity-check script referenced in README.md's 'Verify the math' section) only requires public/calc.js and never reads public/rates.json, so it validates against whatever is hardcoded in calc.js, not what ships to users.

If a future edit updates rates.json without updating calc.js's matching literals (or vice versa), verify.js will report numbers that don't match the live site, defeating its purpose as a trust check. Currently they happen to agree, but nothing enforces that.

Fix: have verify.js JSON.parse public/rates.json and call calc.applyRates(json) before calc.analyze(), same as app.js does. Optionally add a startup assertion that calc.RATES values equal the rates.json values post-merge, so future edits that only touch one file fail loudly instead of drifting silently.
issue.title: verify.js doesn't load rates.json -- Node verification can silently diverge from the live site

detail.reason: Fixed verify.js to load public/rates.json and call calc.applyRates() before analysis, matching the live browser tool's runtime behavior. This ensures Node verification validates against the same rate data that users see, preventing silent divergence if future edits update rates.json without updating calc.js defaults. Added a startup assertion that warns when rates.json values differ from baked-in defaults, making drift visible during verification.

Added FAQPage JSON-LD structured data to public/index.html. The JSON-LD script mirrors all 4 Q&A pairs from the visible FAQ section (Time-of-Use, Steady Use/Smart Energy, EV rate, data privacy). Google can now render these as expandable rich-result snippets for relevant search queries, potentially increasing organic click-through.

Added Cloudflare Web Analytics (cookie-less, privacy-safe) to measure site usage. Tracking implemented: pageviews + custom events for sample button clicks, successful parses, and parse errors. Updated README.md and footer to document analytics collection. The beacon script is in place with a placeholder token that needs to be replaced with the actual Cloudflare Web Analytics token from the dashboard.

Implemented opt-in SmartCharge NY /bin/bash.10/kWh off-peak credit for the TOU model, UI toggle, plan-table/math breakdown, and eligibility caveat; verified with the existing suite and targeted EV math.

Implemented staleness warning for rates.json - added reviewedThrough field (2026-07-01) and display warning banner when rates are 6+ months old, making staleness visible to end users without external monitoring

Push-to-deploy successfully wired for coned-rate-optimizer via website-build Argo sensor per ADR-001. All steps completed: bootstrap runner removed, Forgejo webhook registered, sensor configuration fixed, and deployment verified with test commit.

Added automated test suite and committed sample Green Button CSV fixture. test/test.js covers 16 tests (parsing, analysis, rate calculations, edge cases) and verify.js now runs successfully from a clean checkout. All tests passing (16/16).
